title: Spot the bug
prompt:
What happens when you call `f(3)`?
`public int f(int n) { return n + f(n - 1); }`
options: StackOverflowError — there's no base case, so it recurses forever
explanation: Nothing ever stops the recursion: f(3) → f(2) → f(1) → f(0) → f(-1) → ... until the call stack runs out. Base case first, always.

title: Fibonacci skeleton
prompt: Complete the classic (inefficient but canonical) recursive Fibonacci.
explanation: fib(0)=0 and fib(1)=1, which `return n` covers in one line. Each call branches into two — that exponential blowup is exactly what dynamic programming will fix later.

title: Power, recursively
prompt: Return `base` raised to `exp` (exp ≥ 0) using recursion, not `Math.pow`. Base case: anything to the 0th power is 1. Recursive case: `base * power(base, exp - 1)`.

solution.explanation: The return type is `long` because 2^40 overflows int. (Fast exponentiation halves exp instead — an optimization you'll meet later.)

title: Drill: recursive digit count
prompt: From memory: return the number of digits in `n` (n ≥ 0) recursively. Base case: `n < 10` has 1 digit. Otherwise: 1 + digits of `n / 10`.
hints: Base case handles 0-9 in one line.
